newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe raises fuel prices by 6-8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe raises fuel prices by 6-8 percent.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government raised the price of petrol and other fuel by between six and eight percent on Tuesday, citing higher operational and procurement costs for its third price increase this year.
The rise was announced in a statement by Transport and Energy Minister Simon Moyo.

"The increases have been necessitated by changes in the FOB (Free On Board) prices that have risen significantly due to recent missile attacks of Iraq by the United States as well as increases in operating costs," he said.
The retail cost of petrol goes up six percent to Z$4.15 (40 U.S. cents) from Z$3.91 (38 cents) a litre, and diesel rises to Z$3.31 (32 cents) from Z$3.08 (30 cents) a litre.
Aviation fuel now costs Z$4.26 (41 cents) from Z$4.00 (39 cents) a litre, and paraffin rises eight percent to Z$1.48 (14 cents) from Z$1.37 (13 cents) a litre.
